newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel unchanged against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel unchanged against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed unchanged against the dollar on Thursday despite the overnight decline of the U.S. currency against the mark and yen in Asian markets, dealers said.

"During the day the shekel rose slightly following dollar's decline in Asia but the representative rate was set unchanged as the central bank uses the highest price to calculate the rate," said Israel Sapir of Bank Leumi.

"The basket continues to remain at the lower edge of the trading band. The central bank had to intervene several times in the market to support the basket as investors continue to take foreign currency-linked loans," Sapir said.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
Dealers estimated that the Bank of Israel bought more than $100 million in foreign currency on Thursday.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3120 shekels, unchanged from Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6265 shekels against 3.6255 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7185 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7119 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.0190 shekels against 2.0174 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3080 shekels.
